question: Does the current TRL AsyncGRPO RolloutQueueDataset admit only part of one logical prompt group when the policy version advances between reads, because staleness is evaluated per sample?

estimand.atomicity_contract: For samples emitted from a single logical GRPO prompt group, stale admission should be all-or-none if the trainer claims complete-group consumption. The issue proposes retaining rollout identity and sequence membership to allow complete rollout admission before packing.
estimand.tested_behavior: The production RolloutQueueDataset iterator's per-sample admission decision across a policy-version transition.
estimand.not_tested: No optimizer update, group-relative gradient, real async worker, distributed execution, or task-success effect.

method.independent_fixture: VARE-authored Python fixture with three queued samples sharing a group_id and model_version=0; consume one at current version 0, advance the callback-visible current version to 1, then observe remaining rows under max_staleness=0. A current-version sentinel bounds iteration.
method.control: With no policy-version transition, all three same-group rows must be yielded.

failure_criteria: The pinned source revision or either relevant source-file hash differs.
The fixed-version control does not yield all three rows.
The transition case does not show partial same-group admission and stale drops.
The reproducer requires a GPU, model download, external service, or paid resource.
claim_boundary: A queue-iterator counterexample under an explicit all-or-none group-admission contract. It does not establish a wrong optimizer update, training prevalence, or model capability impact.
